title: Batched Webhook Contracts for Large Payloads and Backpressure Handling
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:

This integration guide defines the contract, operational controls, and recommended implementation patterns for integrating customer endpoints that receive batched webhooks containing large payloads. It is intended for platform engineers, integration engineers on customer teams, and Customer Success engineers who coordinate go-lives. The goal is to minimize dropped traffic, bound memory/CPU cost at the receiver, and ensure predictable retry/backpressure behavior across Redwood hosted and Dedicated/Private environments.

Audience:
- Customer Success (CS) and Solutions Engineers
- Integration/Platform Engineers at customer organizations
- Redwood SREs responsible for ingress proxies and client libraries

Why this exists:
- Customers frequently need batched delivery to reduce per-request overhead for high-throughput use cases (e.g., embedding sync, event batches, document uploads).
- Large payloads (>256 KB) amplify failure modes: slow receivers, head-of-line blocking, and unexpected client memory spikes.
- Without an explicit contract, different clients interpret retries/backoff differently leading to cascading load and downtime.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to: webhook-style delivery (HTTP/HTTPS) from Redwood integration proxies to customer-owned endpoints used during onboarding and production flows.
- Not covered: pure streaming (gRPC) integrations or in-band synchronous inference responses. See streaming-webhook guide for streaming semantics.

Key definitions (used in this guide):
- Batch: a single HTTP POST containing an array of records/events/documents.
- Payload size: total bytes of the request body, after compression if compression negotiation is used.
- Delivery window: time period within which Redwood will attempt retries before handing the message to dead-letter or escalation flows.
- Backpressure token: short-lived header (X-RWBP-Token) issued by the receiver to indicate temporary capacity constraints.

Contract: request and response expectations

Required request headers:
- Content-Type: application/json
- X-RW-Tenant: <tenant-id> (mandatory for Dedicated/Private routing)
- X-RW-Batch-Count: <integer> (number of items in this batch)
- X-RW-Batch-Bytes: <integer> (uncompressed size in bytes)
- X-RW-Id: <uuid> (idempotency key for the batch)
- Accept-Encoding: gzip (supported, optional)

Recommended (optional) headers:
- X-RW-Prefetch: <estimated-items-ahead> (used by receivers to tune prefetch/buffers)

Response codes and semantics:
- 200 OK: Full acceptance. Redwood considers batch delivered; no retries. Body may contain a JSON acknowledgment mapping ids to per-item statuses (see per-item ack format below).
- 202 Accepted: Receiver accepted batch for asynchronous processing. Redwood treats as success (no retry).
- 429 Too Many Requests: Receiver is asking the sender to slow down. Must include Retry-After (seconds) header or X-RW-Backoff (ms). Redwood will respect Retry-After and fall back to exponential backoff.
- 503 Service Unavailable: Temporary capacity problem. Must include Retry-After or X-RW-Backoff. Redwood will attempt retry according to configured retry window and failover policies.
- 4xx (other): Permanent client errors (e.g., malformed payload). Redwood will surface to customer and not retry.
- 5xx: Transient server error. Redwood will perform retries and escalate per escalation policy if persistent.

Per-item acknowledgment format (optional body on 200):
- If receiver wants to indicate partial acceptance, return 200 with JSON: { "id_statuses": [{"id": "<item-id>", "status": "accepted|rejected|retry", "reason": "optional human text" } ] }
- Redwood will retry only items marked "retry" or missing from id_statuses when configured for fine-grained retries. Coarse-grained integrations should return full 200/202 and avoid partial acceptance.

Payload sizing and batching constraints (default recommended):
| Threshold | Value | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Recommended max batch items | 200 | Prevent large CPU/JSON parse spikes on receivers |
| Recommended max batch bytes (uncompressed) | 8,388,608 (8 MB) | Soft recommendation; verify with customer during onboarding |
| Hard max batch bytes (policy) | 16,777,216 (16 MB) | Redwood will reject >16MB with 413 Payload Too Large unless negotiated |
| Preferred per-item size for stability | < 512 KB | Items larger than this should be split or uploaded separately

Negotiating larger payloads: multipart upload handshake
- For sustained use-cases requiring items >512KB or batches >8MB, customers should implement a two-phase handshake:
  1) Receiver responds with 202 and X-RW-Upload-Url: pre-signed URL for multipart upload (S3 or Azure blob allowed).
  2) Redwood will upload large blobs to the provided URL and then POST a trimmed batch with references (blob ids/URLs) instead of inlining payloads.
- Handshake failures should be returned as 4xx/5xx accordingly; Redwood will retry the batch flow but not the individual large-blob uploads unless the receiver accepts them.

Backpressure and flow control mechanism
- Short-term backpressure: receiver returns 429 or 503 with Retry-After in seconds or X-RW-Backoff in milliseconds. Redwood will:
  - Respect Retry-After and pause pushes to that endpoint for the duration plus jitter.
  - Gradually ramp down parallel connections (min connection limit = 1, not 0) then attempt slow probe requests.
- Token-based capacity signaling (recommended):
  - Receiver may issue an X-RWBP-Token header in responses (value valid for 30s). When set, Redwood reduces concurrency to the level encoded in the token metadata (opaque to Redwood). Tokens are advisory and used to coordinate multi-proxy setups.
- Long-term flow control: If an endpoint repeatedly signals backpressure (more than N times within M minutes), Redwood will move the tenant to an adaptive-fanout queue and notify the CS owner for remediation.

Retry policy (default, overridable by customer contract)
1) Immediate retries: on 5xx up to 2 immediate attempts, 200ms apart.
2) Exponential backoff: initial 1s, multiplier 2, max interval 60s. Total retry window default 15 minutes for individual batches.
3) For TTL-sensitive messages (configurable flag in integration manifest), total retry window reduced to 90 seconds.
4) After exhausting retry window, Redwood will:
  - Move batch to tenant-specific dead-letter queue (DLQ) for inspection, AND
  - Trigger CS escalation per the escalation matrix below.

Observability contract: metrics and traces the receiver must expose/emit during onboarding
- Required telemetry for onboarding:
  - DeliverySuccessRate (per tenant, per endpoint)
  - AvgProcessingLatency (p50/p95) measured from initial receipt to 202/200 response
  - CurrentQueueDepth or PendingJobs (if asynchronous processing)
- Redwood will correlate traces using the X-RW-Id and a trace header X-RW-Trace-Id (if present). Customers should log/emit the trace id in request processing logs.

Integration test checklist (onboarding preflight)
1) Basic handshake: Redwood POSTs a batch of 10 small items, endpoint returns 200.
2) Partial acceptance: return per-item ack and verify Redwood retries only expected items.
3) Backpressure simulation: return 429 with Retry-After=30 and confirm Redwood respects the pause.
4) Large payload: send a single 1.5 MB item and verify multipart handshake path completes.
5) Rate flood: simulate burst of 500 batches in 60s and confirm receiver CPU/heap remains within expected bounds.
6) Observability: confirm DeliverySuccessRate and AvgProcessingLatency are visible in both Redwood console and customer dashboards.

Operational runbook and escalation matrix
- Owners:
  - Redwood CS Integration Lead: Maya Chen (primary)
  - Redwood SRE Oncall: eng-sre team (pager)
  - Customer Engineering POC: named during onboarding
- Escalation steps (automated and manual):
  1) Automated: If DeliverySuccessRate < 95% for 5 consecutive minutes, send automated alert and open a P1 incident in Redwood PagerDuty.
  2) CS outreach: CS Integration Lead pages customer POC and opens joint debugging session.
  3) Platform mitigation: SRE may route affected tenant to a buffered DLQ/fanout layer, temporarily reducing direct push traffic.
  4) Executive: If outage extends beyond 2 hours and impacts SLA, CS and Sales notify customer execs and prepare credit/mitigation plan.

Rollout/canary guidance for customers
- Start with a small tenant sample of 1–5% of traffic.
- Enforce a hard peek-limit: max 1 connection and 1 batch/second during initial 24h.
- Gradually increase by doubling traffic every 24 hours while monitoring AvgProcessingLatency and server heap usage.

Examples and code snippets
- Example POST body (compact):
{
  "batch_id": "4c2b8a56-...",
  "items": [ {"id": "i1", "payload": "..."}, {"id": "i2", "payload": "..."} ]
}

- Example 429 response (recommended headers):
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 30
X-RW-Backoff: 30000
Content-Type: application/json
{ "message": "temporarily overloaded, try after 30s" }

- Example partial ack 200 body:
{ "id_statuses": [{"id": "i1", "status": "accepted"}, {"id": "i2", "status": "retry", "reason": "transient db lock"}] }

FAQ (short)
- Q: What if my endpoint cannot handle batches but can handle many small requests?
  A: Negotiate smaller batch sizes (items <= 20, bytes <= 256KB) and increase concurrency at the receiver side. We can configure Redwood to send more parallel requests instead of large batches.
- Q: Do you support mutual TLS?
  A: Yes. During Dedicated/Private onboarding, mutual TLS and pinned certificates are supported. See onboarding checklist to exchange certs.
- Q: What happens to items lost after retries?
  A: Items that exhaust retries land in a tenant DLQ and are available to the customer for inspection and re-ingestion. The CS team will coordinate DLQ access.

Appendix: configuration knobs (examples to share with customer)
- inbound.max_batch_bytes = 8388608
- inbound.max_items_per_batch = 200
- delivery.retry_window_seconds = 900
- delivery.immediate_retries = 2
- delivery.initial_backoff_ms = 1000

This guide should be applied during Dedicated and Private tenant onboarding by default and offered as an integration option for Hosted customers with high-throughput ingestion patterns. For implementation help, contact the CS Integration Lead or open a ticket routed to the integration squad.
